detections.evidence_quote: Okay tonight we are doing a deep dive on sleep hygiene because so many people wrote in asking for it.
detections.summary: Deep dive on sleep hygiene: bedroom temperature, darkness, noise, consistent timing, caffeine, alcohol, exercise, screens, naps, bedding, meals and wind-down routines.

detections.evidence_quote: going to bed and waking up around the same time every day, weekends included, trains your body's internal clock.
detections.summary: Going to bed and waking at the same time daily, weekends included, is said to train the body's internal clock.

detections.evidence_quote: Caffeine timing matters a lot too, it can linger in your system for six or more hours depending on the person.
detections.summary: Caffeine can linger six or more hours, so an afternoon coffee may still affect sleep at night.

detections.evidence_quote: Alcohol is another one, people think it helps them fall asleep, and it might, but it fragments sleep later in the night.
detections.summary: Alcohol may help people fall asleep but fragments sleep, causing more waking in the second half of the night.

detections.evidence_quote: Exercise earlier in the day tends to help sleep quality, but intense exercise right before bed can rev some people up too much.
detections.summary: Exercise earlier in the day tends to help sleep quality while intense exercise right before bed can rev people up.

detections.evidence_quote: As a board certified sleep physician, I have seen this pattern in my own patients over and over again in the clinic.
detections.summary: Guest invokes being a board certified sleep physician and seeing the pattern in their own patients.

detections.evidence_quote: doom scrolling keeps your brain alert right when it should be winding down.
detections.summary: Screens before bed are said to disrupt sleep through both light and stimulation, with doom scrolling keeping the brain alert.

detections.evidence_quote: that combination seems to help a lot of my patients specifically.
detections.summary: A cooler room with a heavier blanket is supported by what helps the guest's patients.

detections.evidence_quote: I have one and I genuinely do not know how I slept without it before, it feels like a permanent hug.
detections.summary: Speaker's own weighted blanket experience is offered after the general claim that weighted blankets calm people.

detections.evidence_quote: Diet can play a role too, a heavy or spicy meal too close to bedtime can cause discomfort that keeps people up.
detections.summary: Heavy or spicy meals and lots of liquid close to bedtime are said to disrupt sleep through discomfort and night-time bathroom trips.

detections.evidence_quote: Anxiety about sleep itself is a huge factor too, lying there stressing about not sleeping tends to make it worse.
detections.summary: Anxiety about not sleeping worsens it; getting out of bed and reserving the bed for sleep strengthens the bed-sleep association.

detections.evidence_quote: consistency with the boring stuff beats any single trick almost every time in my experience.
detections.summary: Guest supports the point that consistent habits beat single tricks with their own experience.

verification_candidates.rationale: Causal claim about late napping and sleep onset.

verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Same with a lot of liquid right before bed, that is just going to mean a trip to the bathroom at two in the morning.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Stressing about not sleeping while lying in bed tends to make sleep worse.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: lying there stressing about not sleeping tends to make it worse.
verification_candidates.rationale: Causal claim about sleep anxiety and insomnia.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Getting out of bed when unable to sleep, such as reading a boring magazine in dim light in another room for fifteen minutes before trying again, can help some people sleep.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Reading a boring magazine in dim light in another room for fifteen minutes and then trying again can actually help some people.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Keeping the bedroom just for sleeping, not for work or scrolling, seems to reinforce the association between bed and sleep over time.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Consistency with basic sleep habits beats any single sleep trick almost every time.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: consistency with the boring stuff beats any single trick almost every time in my experience.
verification_candidates.rationale: Comparative claim about sleep interventions grounded in clinical experience.
